rv.q: The sheer number of cringe-making appropriations in “Takes All Kinds” tends to eclipse the content.
Hoyle has distilled what he heard from the folks he met into 70 not-to-be-missed minutes — sometimes rollickingly funny, sometimes profoundly on point.

cn.t: Critics are split on Dan Hoyle's solo show: one finds it a work of genius empathy, transforming real American voices with rare artistry; another is less convinced. The performance itself draws praise even where the material divides.
